turns.prompt_text: I'm using an Amazon Alexa. Am I able to turn down the volume on The voice only and not the media?
turns.response_html:
You've hit on one of the most common frustrations with Alexa. It feels like she’s shouting over your relaxing music, or conversely, you can’t hear her response because the volume is set low for background noise.

The short answer is: No, there is currently no way to decouple the "System Voice" volume from the "Media" volume. On Amazon Echo devices, the volume control is universal. Whether you turn it up via the physical buttons, the app, or a voice command, it affects everything—music, timers, and Alexa’s own voice—equally.

However, there are a few "quality of life" workarounds that might help make her voice less jarring:

1. Adaptive Volume

This is probably the closest feature to what you're looking for. When enabled, Alexa will analyze the ambient noise in the room and automatically adjust her response volume. If the room is quiet, she'll speak softer; if it's loud, she'll speak up.

  • How to enable: Say, "Alexa, turn on Adaptive Volume."

2. Whisper Mode

If your main issue is that she's too loud at night or in a quiet house, you can use Whisper Mode. If you whisper your command to her, she will whisper her response back, regardless of what the media volume is set to.

  • How to enable: Say, "Alexa, turn on Whisper Mode."

3. Use "Brief Mode"

If you find her voice simply talks too much, Brief Mode makes her responses shorter. Often, she will just play a short "jingle" or chime to confirm a command (like turning off a light) instead of saying "Okay."

  • How to enable: Open the Alexa App > More > Settings > Voice Responses > Toggle on Brief Mode.

4. Routine Workaround (The "Manual" Fix)

If you have a specific time of day where this bothers you (like when you start playing music at night), you can create a Routine in the Alexa app that sets the volume to a specific level (e.g., Level 3) at a certain time, though this still won't separate the two audio streams.

It’s a bit of a design oversight on Amazon's part—especially since many other smart assistants and operating systems keep system sounds and media separate. For now, we're stuck adjusting the "master" slider.
